patches.value: For x∈ℝⁿ and r>0, e(x,r)=‖u_t(x,r)‖₂²+∑_{j=1}^n‖∂_{x_j}u(x,r)‖₂²; the vector norms are Euclidean, and the spatial-gradient term is the Frobenius/Hilbert–Schmidt square of the Jacobian.
For smooth u:ℝⁿ×(0,∞)→ℝᵐ, a differential operator with Δ_xu:ℝⁿ×(0,∞)→ℝᵐ.
For each (x,r), (Δ_xu)(x,r)=∑_{j=1}^n ∂²u(x,r)/∂x_j², with each second derivative taken componentwise in ℝᵐ.

Fix arbitrary r>0 and spatial index j∈Fin n; define v_j=e_j, f_j(x)=∂_{x_j}u(x,r), and g(x)=u_t(x,r). N001 directly supplies a closed time window containing r and a compact C outside which u=q throughout that window. Because u is jointly smooth and is constant on the open set (ℝⁿ\\C)×J, f_j,g and their Frechet derivatives vanish outside C and are continuous. Thus the three functions ⟨Df_j(x)[v_j],g(x)⟩, ⟨f_j(x),Dg(x)[v_j]⟩, and ⟨f_j(x),g(x)⟩ are continuous and supported in C. By M001 and the ambient facts exported in N001, all three are integrable. Smoothness gives the Frechet derivative identities everywhere, in particular on tsupport(g) for f_j and tsupport(f_j) for g. Apply M011 with X=ℝⁿ, F=G=ℝᵐ, W=ℝ, B the Euclidean dot product and direction v_j. It gives ∫⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩=−∫⟨∂_{x_jx_j}u,u_t⟩. Joint smoothness also gives the mixed-partial identity ∂_t∂_{x_j}u=∂_{x_j}u_t used in differentiating the gradient square. Since j was arbitrary, sum these identities over j=1,…,n. The finite-dimensional product rule yields ∫e_t=2∫u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu). N002 identifies E′(r)=∫e_t, proving the desired energy-derivative formula for arbitrary r>0.

value.declaration: At the fixed (x,r), choose the scalar a supplied by H002 so u_{tt}(x,r)−Δ_xu(x,r)=a u(x,r).
